summary: This is a streamlined reimplementation of Cramer's 2011 Kraftwagen, putting players in charge of early American car manufacturers who research engines and bodies, assemble car models, and race them for prestige while managing a rondel of limited actions. Turn order and timing matter a lot, since the rondel forces you to plan several turns ahead and everyone is racing to get desirable engine/body combinations to market before the field is saturated.
praised: thematic tie between engineering and racing
streamlined, less fiddly than the 2011 original
criticised: still fairly dry and mechanical for the theme
rondel can feel restrictive/fiddly to newcomers
market/pricing swings can punish bad timing hard
niche appeal, less known than the designer's bigger hits

interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited technology upgrades and race slots on a shared board, and flooding the market with similar car models depresses everyone's prices, so choices are interdependent even though each player mostly develops their own production line.

subsystems: vehicle manufacturing and sales for money
Grand Prix race results for bonus points
engine/body set collection for bonus points
sources: money earned from selling manufactured cars
scoring.how_you_win: You win by ending with the most points/money, built mainly from designing and selling successful car models over the game's rounds, topped up with bonuses from strong Grand Prix showings and completed vehicle sets.
